info.name: BytePlus Seedance 2.5
info.description:
Every Seedance request type, ready to run.

## Setup

Set the `ARK_API_KEY` collection variable to your ModelArk key. Nothing else is required — the sample assets are BytePlus's own public documentation samples, so every request works as-is.

## How it flows

Any request that submits successfully stores its task id in `TASK_ID`, so **Task management → Get task** polls whatever you just sent. Repeat it every 10–15s until the status is terminal.

## Seedance 2.5 in one paragraph

Requests fall into five task types. Text-to-video and reference-to-video have no special constraints. First-frame, video-edit and video-extend all lock the output ratio to their source (`ratio` must be `adaptive`), and an edit additionally locks the duration (`duration` must be `-1`).

The catch: edit and extend are classified from your PROMPT, not your parameters, and that happens after the task queues — so a clash normally surfaces minutes later as a failed, already-billed task. Declaring `omni_reference_task_type` moves that check to submit time. The 'Constraint errors' folder demonstrates it.

Generated by scripts/generate_postman_collection.py — request bodies come from executing the SDK, so they cannot drift from the code.

item.name: 5 · Constraint errors

request.description:
An edit inherits ratio and duration from the source, so neither may be set.

This is the payoff of declaring the task type: WITHOUT `omni_reference_task_type` the identical request is accepted, queues, consumes a billed slot, and only then fails with InvalidParameter.TaskTypeConstraint. Declared, it fails here at submit and no task is created.
Extension locks the ratio to the source. Duration, unlike an edit, is free.
An edit needs something to edit. The reply says 'exactly one reference video', but that describes the semantic — the model edits one video, selected from the inputs — not a cap: several ARE allowed.
The API lists the permitted values in its error, which is a handy way to confirm the enum: auto, reference, edit, extend.
Seedance 2.5 offers 480p and 720p only. For a higher-resolution master, generate at 720p and upscale, or switch to Seedance 2.0.
